newsitem.title: CHINA: Two Korean Red Cross societies begin talks on aid.
newsitem.headline: Two Korean Red Cross societies begin talks on aid.

text.p: The Red Cross societies of rival North and South Korea started talks on Wednesday in Beijing to discuss more food aid for the North, on the brink of starvation after years of economic disintegration.
"The talks have started," South Korean embassy spokesman Chang Moon Ik said.
The negotiations follow talks in Beijing in May when the South Korean Red Cross pledged 50,000 tonnes of grain aid for the Stalinist North. That shipment is due to be completed later this month.
Officials of the North and South Red Cross societies declined to comment on details of the talks, and South Korean embassy spokesman Chang said discussions could last several days.
"We will have to see what is decided today," Chang said. "Maybe they will continue on Friday."
The previous talks, the first between the two sides for nearly five years, focused in part on delivery of the aid, with the South insisting the grain be clearly labelled as coming from South Korea.
The South also demanded guarantees the food aid would not be diverted into the hands of Pyongyang's military.

International aid workers say the communist North is on the brink of famine after floods in 1995 and 1996 devastated much of the country's farmland and industrial bases, exacerbating already severe food shortages in the hermit nation.

The latest discussions were agreed to earlier this month when an offer by the South to hold talks for further food aid on the Korean peninsula was met with a counter-proposal by the northern Red Cross to hold the meeting in Beijing.
The Red Cross is the only legal channel for private aid from South Korea to the North.
The aid agreed last May came on top of $16 million worth of donations made by Seoul in response to an appeal by the United Nations World Food Programme.
Washington also this month nearly doubled its total food aid to North Korea to $52 million, intended to combat widespread malnutrition, particularly among children.
